subject.title: [Bug]: Preflight compaction failure permanently locks Composer into "terminated" state

question: Which candidate and retryability contract should own this issue: the narrowed runtime guard, a UI lifecycle recovery path, or another combined approach?
rationale: Current main is still broken, but the open PRs differ on the provider-error boundary and prior maintainer feedback rejected broad 4xx fail-open behavior; automation should not choose the permanent failure policy without owner intent.

options.title: Use narrowed runtime guard
options.body: Pick one canonical PR that skips timeout, true 429 rate-limit, and 5xx only, requires 400/401/403 plus billing-429 negative controls, and asks for real chat proof before merge.

options.title: Use UI recovery instead
options.body: Keep preflight compaction failures terminal in the runtime and repair Control UI/Gateway lifecycle recovery so pre-run dispatch errors show an actionable error and restore retry.

options.title: Combine runtime and UI safeguards
options.body: Land the narrowed runtime guard first and add UI recovery as a follow-up only if real proof still shows Composer lockout on a remaining compaction failure path.

recommendation.title: Use narrowed runtime guard
recommendation.body: Pick one canonical PR that skips timeout, true 429 rate-limit, and 5xx only, requires 400/401/403 plus billing-429 negative controls, and asks for real chat proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc gave the concrete retryability-boundary feedback referenced by the reporter and is tied to adjacent compaction/error history.
